newsitem.title: italy: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS ANOTHER BUTTERFLY WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV SETS ANOTHER BUTTERFLY WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Russia's double Olympic champion Denis Pankratov set his second short-course world record in less than a week on Wednesday when he clocked 51.93 seconds for the 100 metres butterfly at a World Cup meeting.

The previous best had stood for almost seven years, although Pankratov himself swam faster in Paris last year only to be denied the record because French meet organisers had run out of bottles to administer the dope tests necessary for ratification.
Marcel Gery of Canada set the old mark of 52.07 in Leicester, England, on February 23, 1990.

Pankratov is the first man to hold all four butterfly world records since Michael Gross -- 100 and 200 long-course (50-metre pool) and short-course (25-metre pool). Wednesday's world mark was the first set at the two-day World Cup meeting in Imperia, northwest Italy.

Pankratov last Saturday clocked one minute 52.64 seconds in the 200 butterfly at another World Cup meeting in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, to beat the previous best of 1:53.05 set by Frenchman Franck Esposito in Paris in February 1994.
Almost exactly a year ago Pankratov clocked 51.94 in the 100 butterfly and 1:52.34 in the 200 butterfly at the Paris World Cup meeting where the dope test fiasco occurred.
